title: Runtime LTS: Known Issues and Explicit Exclusions
author: Samir Qureshi
body:
## Purpose
This page is the **living list** of:
- **Known issues** in the Runtime LTS channel (current focus: `runtime-1.20-lts` line)
- **Explicit exclusions** (capabilities we do *not* support or do *not* guarantee in LTS)

It exists to reduce upgrade surprises for Dedicated/Private/Enterprise customers and to make LTS release notes “operationally quiet” by linking here for long-running caveats.

**Audience:** Runtime, Release Engineering, SRE, Support/CS, and enterprise operators.

---
## What “LTS” means (in this context)
LTS patches aim for **minimal behavioral change**. Patch content is generally limited to:
- Security fixes
- Correctness fixes
- Stability improvements
- Narrow, targeted performance regression fixes (with strong evidence)

LTS does **not** promise feature parity with mainline nor support for every model/config combination.

---
## How to use this page
- **Before requesting a backport:** confirm the issue isn’t already listed here as “known / accepted” or “excluded.”
- **Before upgrading (Private/Dedicated):** review the “Known perf cliffs / operational caveats” section.
- **When writing LTS release notes:** include a “Known issues” link and call out any change in status (New / Resolved / Worsened).

Support note: When responding to enterprise tickets, link to the relevant section and include the **scope** (model family, hardware, quantization, context length, runtime config).

---
## Status legend
- **New:** first published in the last two patch cycles
- **Active:** still reproducible / not fixed in current LTS patch
- **Mitigated:** workaround exists; fix not planned for the current LTS line
- **Resolved:** fixed in an LTS patch (include version)
- **Excluded:** not eligible for LTS support/backport (see exclusions)

---
## Known Issues (LTS)
The table below is intended to be “operator-friendly.” It emphasizes symptoms, triggers, impact, and mitigations.

| ID | Status | Area | Symptom / Impact | Trigger / Scope | Mitigation / Workaround | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| KI-001 | Active | Scheduler | **Tail latency spikes** (p99) under mixed short+long requests; can cause brief queue growth | High concurrency + wide prompt length distribution; most visible with `continuous_batching=on` and `max_batch_tokens` > 64k | Pin `max_batch_tokens` to 32k–48k; enable length-bucketing (`scheduler.length_buckets=true`) in Private; monitor `scheduler_queue_wait_ms` | Under investigation for minimal-diff fix; avoid large scheduler refactors in LTS (see Exclusions) |
| KI-002 | Mitigated | KV cache | **Elevated memory use** leading to early OOM or increased eviction rate; throughput drops | Long-context workloads (8k–16k+) on GPUs with smaller HBM (e.g., 40GB) + high `max_concurrent_sequences` | Reduce `max_concurrent_sequences`; enable `kv_cache.compaction=on`; set `kv_cache.max_bytes` explicitly; prefer 80GB for 16k contexts | Not considered a “regression” if within published sizing guidance; still commonly misconfigured |
| KI-003 | Active | Quantization | **Quality regressions** reported for some code-gen prompts when using `int4` profiles | `int4` weight-only quantization on certain model families; especially when temperature < 0.3 | Use `int8` or FP16/BF16 for sensitive routes; if staying on int4, raise temperature slightly and validate with eval set | LTS guarantees stability of runtime behavior, not prompt-level quality across quantization profiles |
| KI-004 | Active | Multi-node | **Occasional deadlock** during tensor-parallel init; requires pod restart | Multi-node Private deployments using NCCL over constrained east-west networking; more frequent after node recycle | Ensure NCCL health checks enabled; set `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME` to dedicated interface; increase init timeout; keep `hostNetwork` consistent | Considered an infra+runtime interaction; fix may land in mainline first and be evaluated for backport |
| KI-005 | New | Observability | **Trace sampling changes** can make token-level traces appear “missing” for low-QPS services | Low traffic + default sampling + short-lived pods; especially on canaries | Set explicit `tracing.sample_rate` for canary environments; confirm collector retention; use request logs for verification | Not a functional regression; impacts debugging workflows |
| KI-006 | Active | Tool calling / structured output | **Streaming tool-call frames** may flush slightly later than expected, impacting UI responsiveness | Streaming enabled + high server-side batching | For UI-first routes, reduce `target_batching_delay_ms`; consider disabling streaming tool-calls for latency-critical endpoints | Fix likely requires deeper scheduler changes; not guaranteed for current LTS line |
| KI-007 | Mitigated | Compilation / kernels | **First-request latency** higher than expected after pod restart | Cold start + compilation cache miss (Private with ephemeral volumes) | Persist compilation cache volume; pre-warm with a canary job; ensure image includes precompiled kernels for pinned models | LTS release notes should continue to call out cache persistence requirement |

---
## Known Performance Cliffs / Operational Caveats
These are not always “bugs,” but they are common sources of enterprise incidents.

1) **Context length cliffs (step-function behavior)**
- Symptom: near-linear latency up to a point, then sharp p95/p99 increase and/or throughput collapse.
- Typical causes: crossing attention kernel boundary, KV cache paging/eviction, or hitting `max_batch_tokens` pressure.
- What to do:
  - Keep maximum prompt+generation lengths within validated bands for your GPU class.
  - Avoid mixing extremely long and extremely short requests in the same route without length bucketing.
  - Use separate routes/models for long-context workloads.

2) **Small-batch inefficiency at very low QPS**
- Symptom: high per-token cost and higher latency than expected at <1–2 RPS.
- Cause: continuous batching has less opportunity to form efficient batches.
- What to do: enable prefix caching where applicable; consider smaller model variants; consider dedicated route-level min batching delay.

3) **NUMA/PCIe placement sensitivity (on-prem)**
- Symptom: large variance between “identical” servers.
- Cause: CPU affinity and PCIe topology differences can affect GPU feed and NCCL performance.
- What to do: follow Private deployment host-tuning guide; pin CPU affinity for runtime worker; validate with benchmark-lab baseline.

---
## Explicit Exclusions (Not Supported / Not Guaranteed in LTS)
These exclusions apply to the LTS channel even if the functionality exists in mainline or is “best effort” elsewhere. Exclusions are meant to reduce ambiguity during enterprise escalations.

### 1) Model family / capability exclusions
The following are **excluded** from LTS support guarantees unless explicitly stated in a customer SOW:
- **Multimodal models** (vision/audio) and multimodal pre/post processing in the runtime.
- **Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)** architectures where routing behavior materially changes across minor runtime versions.
- **Very long context** beyond LTS-validated bands (e.g., >16k tokens) unless the specific model+GPU pair is called out in the LTS release notes.
- **Experimental decoding modes** (speculative decoding variants, advanced guided decoding modes) not listed as “stable” in the LTS overview.

### 2) Configuration exclusions (unsupported combinations)
- Combining **int4** quantization with **tool calling + streaming** on certain models is considered “best effort” (see KI-003/KI-006).
- **Custom CUDA extensions** or out-of-tree kernel patches in customer images.
- Non-standard **NCCL builds** not shipped/validated by Redwood (Private on-prem).

### 3) Change-type exclusions (what we won’t backport into LTS)
Per backport policy, the following are generally **not eligible** for LTS patches:
- Broad refactors of scheduler, batching, KV cache architecture, or memory allocator
- Feature work (new APIs, new config surfaces) unless required for security/compliance
- Changes with ambiguous performance impact or that require “tuning” to avoid regressions
- Large dependency upgrades (CUDA major/minor, NCCL major, compiler toolchain) unless required for a security fix and approved by Release Eng + Security

### 4) Guarantees we do not make in LTS
- We do not guarantee prompt-level output parity across **quantization profiles**.
- We do not guarantee performance improvements; we guarantee **no material regression** against the LTS baseline within defined thresholds (see SRE gates).
- We do not guarantee that every mainline fix will be backported; backports require risk assessment and evidence.

---
## Escalation guidance (Support/CS + Runtime)
When a customer reports an issue on LTS:
1) Confirm the customer is on an **LTS artifact** (exact tag + build provenance) and provide:
   - Runtime version (e.g., `runtime-1.20-lts.2`)
   - Deployment mode (Dedicated / Private VPC / on-prem)
   - GPU type + driver
   - Model name + quantization profile
   - Request pattern (prompt length distribution, QPS, streaming on/off)
2) Check this page:
   - If listed as **Active/Mitigated**, provide the workaround and capture whether it resolves.
   - If it matches an **Exclusion**, set expectations and propose supported alternatives (different model/profile/config).
3) If not listed, open a Runtime escalation with:
   - Minimal reproducer (prompt set or synthetic generator)
   - Logs/metrics screenshots (p95/p99, error rate, OOM, queue wait)
   - Whether issue is a regression vs. last LTS patch

Suggested routing:
- Correctness/stability: Runtime oncall → Omar El-Sayed (backport owner)
- Perf regressions vs baseline: SRE gate owner (Sean Gallagher) + Runtime perf (Kira Volkov)
- Artifact/provenance concerns: Release Eng (Connor O’Brien / Sahana Iyer)

---
## Update cadence and ownership
- **Owner:** Serving Runtime (Stability)
- **Maintainer:** Samir Qureshi
- **Review cadence:** at minimum once per LTS patch cycle; additionally within 48 hours of any Sev2+ incident attributable to LTS runtime.

Change rules:
- New entries must include: symptom, trigger/scope, mitigation, and whether it is backport-eligible.
- Resolved entries must cite the **first LTS patch version** where resolved.
- Exclusions require Runtime LTS architect approval (Noah Patel) and must be aligned with the LTS overview page.

- 2026-02-10: Added KI-005 (trace sampling caveat) and clarified exclusions for MoE/multimodal.
- 2026-01-18: Added scheduler p99 spikes (KI-001) mitigation guidance and expanded perf cliff notes.
